title: The library that lends tools
paragraphs: A. The library on North Street lends out tools as well as books. Members can borrow things such as a drill, a sewing machine or a set of gardening tools. A standard loan lasts seven days. If nobody else has booked the equipment, a member can ask for one renewal. The aim is to help people complete small jobs at home without buying items they may use only once.

B. People register at the main desk. A library card is enough for most requests, but powered tools require a ten-minute safety introduction. This introduction is given at the workbench on Saturday mornings. Participants learn to check a cable for damage and find the stop switch before switching the tool on.

C. The library does not buy every new item itself. Some residents donate equipment, and a volunteer team checks each donation before accepting it. The team rejects items it cannot repair or replace safely. It keeps a record of the checks so future volunteers can see what work was done and which parts were changed.

D. During the first three months, sewing machines were borrowed more often than drills. The coordinator expected drills to be the most popular because residents had requested them in a survey. She now plans to collect two kinds of information: how often each tool is borrowed and whether requests are turned down because all copies are out. The second figure should reveal which tools to buy next.

questions.explanation: Đoạn B phân biệt dụng cụ chạy điện và các yêu cầu khác.
choices: Bring a set of replacement parts.

questions.explanation: Đội tình nguyện kiểm tra từng món trước khi nhận.
Bài nêu vai trò kiểm tra của tình nguyện viên, không nêu nghề nghiệp hay bằng cấp.

questions.prompt: Which tools were borrowed more often than drills in the first three months?
questions.explanation: Sewing machines were borrowed more often than drills.

questions.prompt: Why does the coordinator want to count refused requests?
answers: To identify demand that loan records miss.
